purpose: Isolate radiative FP32 arithmetic and photon inversion cost while preserving FP64 trajectory state, elastic/stopping helpers, RNG integer streams and uniform generation.

preflight.notes: Component screening, not a validated whole-transport accuracy bound. Failures remain explicit; safe finite arms may still be timed as unqualified diagnostics.

timing: Fresh processes; one full identical-workload warmup, separate seed +1000000; synchronized boundaries. Alternate variant order each replicate. Preserve full request/reduction and transport intervals separately. No new Nsight counters assumed. CXR execution-call profiling is enabled only in small preflight runs and disabled in all timed pilots. Full fresh-process wall time is retained separately from transport/emission.

ensemble_screen.multiple_comparison: Approximate normal Bonferroni intervals over all scene/population/variant/observable comparisons. Sum of primary-mean SEs bounds unknown cross-precision seed covariance. Zero variance or fewer than 20 scoring primaries leaves source-yield precision unresolved.

exclusions: No production source/default/model marker/version change. No PXR/CBS, no result reuse in transport timing, no extrapolated 100000-primary gain, no qualified cross-engine speedup. Host photon-angle completion remains unchanged FP64 and is included in transport/emission timing.
decisions: Job 1339 retained the initial four-arm preflight, including failures. Its generated CUDA exposed an experimental FP32 exported eV-to-keV constant leaking into the FP64 transport debit; corrected before timing.
Revision 2 keeps the exported unit converter FP64 and uses a separate FP32 constant inside radiative helpers. Adds stable FP32 log1p linear-cell evaluation to compare against selective FP64.
stable_cell_evaluation: Linear chi integral equals chi_left*log1p(x)+slope*left*(x-log1p(x)), x=(right-left)/left. For x<=0.01 evaluate the latter correction through x^6; omitted magnitude <=x^7/7, below FP32 rounding of that correction. No physical tail/grid/model approximation.
